title: Fish and Rice with Tomato-Based Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish “Fish and Rice with Tomato-Based Sauce” combines tender fish, boiled rice, and a fragrant sauce made from tomatoes, onion, garlic, and spices. It is popular in Mediterranean and Asian cuisines, easy to prepare, and suitable for family meals or quick dinners.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomato sauce is rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that gives it a vivid red color.
The fish used is often white (cod, haddock) or oily (salmon, mackerel), influencing the omega‑3 content.
Traditionally, rice is cooked al dente so it holds its shape and doesn’t dissolve into the sauce.
The dish can be made vegetarian by substituting fish with tofu or mushrooms.
In some regions, olives or capers are added to boost flavor.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Oily fish varieties provide omega‑3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Fish and rice together deliver a complete set of essential amino acids for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Lycopene in tomatoes
items.content: Lycopene has antioxidant properties that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Using lean fish and minimal oil keeps the dish light on heart‑unfriendly fats.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Tomatoes, onion, and garlic add vitamin C, potassium, and folate, supporting immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood and should avoid the dish.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking fish can lead to salmonella or listeria growth.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauces often contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Rice glycemic index
items.content: Overcooked rice can raise the glycemic index, which may be undesirable for diabetics.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the fish over rice, drizzled with tomato sauce, and garnish with fresh herbs such as parsley or basil. Pair with a light salad or steamed vegetables. A squeeze of lemon adds a bright acidity.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftovers within 2 hours of cooking and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For freezing, transfer to a freezer‑safe bag and use within 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C.
